title: Structured nutritional intervention for chronic fatigue in patients with primary biliary cholangitis: a cross-sectional and single-blinded randomized controlled clinical trial
summary:
Patients with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) often present with symptoms of fatigue. The underlying mechanisms of fatigue symptoms are still unknown. 
Nutrition could play a role here. In this study, we will measure the effect of malnutrition on fatigue symptoms in patients with PBC and investigate the influence of a structured nutritional intervention.

interventions.name:
Control arm
Patients undergo laboratory and nutrition-related assessments, including body composition analysis and questionnaires on fatigue and quality of life, at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. No structured nutritional intervention is applied.

ntervention arm
Patients undergo laboratory and nutrition-specific assessments, including body composition analysis and questionnaires assessing fatigue and quality of life, at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. A structured nutritional intervention is provided at baseline and at months 3 and 6.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Proven primary biliary cholangitis
Exclusion criteria:
Another autoimmune disease of the liver, which is not primary biliary cholangitis. 
Defibrillator
Structural cardiac diseases
Clinically significant anemia (Hb <9 mg/dl)
Acute inflammation
Active cancer
Depression
Hypothyroidism 
Clinically relevant sleep disorder, defined as ESS >15 points
Lack of consent from the patient
Severe and immediately life-threatening malnutrition in which harm cannot be averted without intervention
